was: Gila NF's most popular Quemado Ranger District campground, on Quemado Lake; 17 RV sites with electric hookups (no sewer) plus leveled tent sites, boat ramp, vault toilets and lake access. Mix of first-come, first-served and reservable (odd-numbered electric sites reservable online); per-site max RV length 35 ft. --Claude
note: Gila NF's most popular Quemado Ranger District campground, on Quemado Lake; 17 RV sites with electric hookups (no sewer) plus leveled tent sites, boat ramp and lake access. Odd-numbered electric sites reservable online. --Claude

was: Santa Fe NF campground of ~39-44 drive-in sites in two loops near the Pecos Wilderness at ~8,900 ft; no hookups, no potable water (new water system pending). Max RV ~25 ft with several sites fitting 23-ft-plus rigs (e.g. site 11), though the approach road (NM-63/FR-555) is narrow. First-come, first-served, open May-Oct. --Claude

was: Carson NF campground in the Valle Vidal unit at ~8,100 ft, reached via ~28 mi of gravel (FR-1950) from Cimarron; 60 sites accommodating trailers to 32 ft, vault toilets, no potable water. First-come, first-served, open mid-spring through fall (Valle Vidal east side closed Jan 1-Mar 31 for elk winter range). --Claude

was: Small Gila NF campground on the Reserve Ranger District, ~6,150 ft in an old-growth ponderosa stand near the Blue Range Wilderness; ~10 sites, no hookups, no potable water, vault toilet. First-come, first-served (not on recreation.gov). RV Life lists max RV ~40 ft, but the 6-mi county access road (C-013) is narrow and winding. --Claude

was: Carson NF campground at ~8,800 ft on the Rio Santa Barbara trout stream, end of FR 116 south of Penasco; 20 sites (15 single + double/triple/quad family sites), vault toilets, drinking-water faucets. Mix of recreation.gov-reservable sites (one pull-through listed to ~40 ft) and FCFS in person. --Claude

was: Gila NF campground on the Reserve Ranger District along FR 141 (Reserve-Beaverhead Rd), ~7,500 ft on South Fork Negrito Creek; 7 sites plus 1 day-use picnic site, most fit trailers to 32 ft, no potable water, first-come first-served. Open year-round; a nearby bridge-replacement project may affect access. --Claude

was: Lincoln NF campground at the base of the White Mountain Wilderness via FR 579 (last 7 of 13 mi unpaved), ~6,350 ft on Three Rivers Creek; 12 rustic sites with table/fire pit/gazebo, RVs to ~25 ft (only a couple fit larger), no potable water, first-come first-served with a year-round host. --Claude

was: 20-site FCFS campground at the upper end of Lake Roberts, Gila NF (Wilderness RD); ponderosa shade, vault toilets, no hookups, self-service fee envelope. Two pull-through sites fit 40-45 ft, the rest cap ~32 ft; reviewers with 21-27 ft trailers (and one 35 ft fifth-wheel) camped fine. Reach it via NM-35 from Mimbres, not NM-15 from Silver City (tight hairpins). Drinking water shut off since a 2024 pipe failure-bring water. --Claude

was: 12 standard nonelectric sites plus a group site in the Magdalena Mountains, Cibola NF (Magdalena RD), ~6,900 ft; vault toilets, picnic table/fire ring/grill at each site, no hookups or water on site. All drive-in; per-site driveways run up to 42 ft with several 27-42 ft sites that fit a mid-size rig, though the final ~500 ft of dirt access road is rough-longer rigs use caution. Mix of first-come and reservable (recreation.gov); FCFS Oct-Mar with possible weather closures. --Claude

was: Small primitive Gila NF campground (Quemado RD) at ~7,850 ft in ponderosa pine off FR 854; 5 FCFS sites with tables and fire rings, FS page notes it can accommodate up to a 35-ft trailer. No hookups, no potable water (unreliable spring), no dump, pack-it-in/pack-it-out, 14-day limit. --Claude

was: Partially-developed FCFS campground at the east end of Quemado Lake, Gila NF (Quemado RD), just east of Pinon CG. Ponderosa and cottonwood along an intermittent stream; popular with hunters and horse campers but open to self-contained RVs up to 32 ft. No water or hookups, pack-it-in/pack-it-out; first-come first-served (nearest dump station at Pinon CG, May-Sep). --Claude

was: FCFS campground on NM-35 near milepost 38 (about 5 mi south of Gila Cliff Dwellings), Gila NF. Overnight camping in the upper cliff-top portion overlooking the West Fork Gila River; the lower riverside portion is day-use only. Vault toilets, no water (nearest water at the Gila Cliff Dwellings visitor center). Accommodates larger RVs (sites used by rigs up to ~38 ft). Not on recreation.gov. --Claude

was: Gila NF campground on the Gila River near Gila Hot Springs (formerly a designated FS campground, now dispersed FCFS). Riverside sites with pit toilets, no potable water, and a swimming hole; the Grapevine-Middle Fork trail leaves into the Gila Wilderness. The posted 20-ft limit reflects the short steep entrance grade off NM-15, not site size — reviewers report Class C rigs to ~29 ft park on the flats by taking it slow. --Claude

was: Gila NF campground along the San Francisco River ~1.5 mi west of Luna off US-180. Five small rustic drive-in sites with tables, fire rings and a vault toilet; no potable water and no trash service (pack it out). First-come, first-served, open year-round. A 25-ft rig parks without issue; rigs over ~35 ft have difficulty at the concrete river ford serving some sites. --Claude

was: City of Lordsburg municipal park offering FCFS overnight RV camping on a large level dirt/gravel lot just off the main road through town. No hookups; 20+ covered picnic ramadas with grills, drinking water, trash dumpster. Level sites fit large rigs (to ~45 ft). Popular I-10 overnight stop. --Claude

was: Village of San Jon municipal recreation park ~1/3 mi S of I-40 in eastern NM (old Route 66 town). FCFS overnight RV camping, ~12-15 level pull-through spots near picnic tables; restrooms, covered picnic area, ballfield, playground. No hookups or showers. Rigs to ~43 ft. --Claude

was: Village of Dexter municipal recreation area on Lake Van, ~15 mi SE of Roswell. Nine numbered electric (30-amp) sites plus dry camping around the lake, big-rig pull-throughs, restrooms, small pool, pavilions; fishing (catfish/trout). FCFS, unmanned office (call for late arrival). --Claude

was: Municipal (Town of Tatum) RV park at 399 E Ash St adjacent to a city park with playground and sports fields. 5 pull-through sites with full hookups (30/50-amp electric, water, sewer), picnic tables, grills, shade trees. Up to 3 nights; first-come, first-served (no reservation system). --Claude

was: Community park/campground in Pie Town (Catron County) on US-60, across from the fire station; hosts the Pie Town festival. Drive-in pull-through and tent sites with dump station and laundry; 7-day stay limit, first-come first-served. Rear sites tighten and get rutted — front sites fit a 23-ft rig. --Claude

was: Small private RV park among oak trees at 121 Mineral Creek Rd, Alma (near Glenwood / Gila NF); ~12 full-hookup 30/50-amp drive-in/pull-through sites, honor-station self-pay, reservation not required (first-come, first-served). --Claude

was: Lower Thames Valley CA campground within a Thames River meander at Morpeth; 48 sites incl. 6 electric (4x30-amp, 2x15-amp w/ water), unserviced traditional sites + 10 backcountry riverfront sites; no dump station; open Victoria Day-Thanksgiving. Reservable online + FCFS. --Claude
